sections.content: Typical introduction to financial accounting course. If you have taken BAFS (accounting module) in DSE, you will have a great advantage since many of the topics are introduced in the DSE such as bad debts, prepayments and accruals. Of course the accounting treatments are slightly different but if you have a solid foundation then it is absolutely easy to understand. New topics can also be expected such as the treatments of bonds and cash flows statements. If you have not taken any accounting courses before, it is better for you to read through the textbook to understand more.
sections.teaching: I registered this lecture only because this session had the shortest waiting list but professor TANG Chao is unexpectedly good. Although it seems that he is not a local professor nor a native English speaker, his English accent is clear and easy to understand. His teaching pace is simply easy to catch up with and he provides examples as well. He explains clearly and will remind you of the main points and common mistakes made by students so as long as you pay attention in class, you will be fine. He will explain again if he thinks a number of students do not understand. Also, he is willing to answer students' questions. In fact, quite many students ask questions in class and he explains one by one patiently. Good choice if you are considering which session to register.
sections.grading: I think the grading is just as usual. If you pay effort and show you understand the topics well, you will do well. You can refer to the mean and median in other comments. I heard that final exams of other professors were also much more difficult than their midterms so it is fair.

There're 8 assignments after class. Usually you have 1 week left to finish it. Each assignment will include 3-4 questions and I think it's okay. Again, you can fool around with these assignments and quizzes, but if you aim high, you should devote your time to this course. sections.content:
Course Roadmap
F/S overview
1. Financial Statements and Business Decisions
2. Investing and Financing Decisions and the Accounting System
3. Operating Decisions and the Accounting System
4. Adjustments, Financial Statements, and the Quality of Earnings
Quiz 1

2. Cost of Goods Sold and Inventory
3. Property, Plant, and Equipment; Intangibles and Natural Resources
4. Liabilities
5. Bond Securities
Quiz 2
SSE, SCF and F/S Analyses
1. Stockholders’ Equity
2. Statement of Cash Flows
3. Analyzing Financial Statements
Final exam

Szu Fan does the in-class exercise with us in class, so just copy all the answers and submit them onto canvas. Sometimes she even sends us the file, and all you have to do is submit what she sends to us. She allows her students to skip one or two assignments I think. Basically everyone can get all 24%.

Class participation is easy to get too. If you answer her question once, you get 3%. So you only have to answer her questions 2 times out of the ENTIRE semester. Once she asked what page we were up to and gave the student 3% who answered her. She tells the whole class it is "participation mark time" before asking, so make sure you don't fall asleep in class and miss the chance. By the last few lessons, she only asks students who haven't got full credit, so all students can score full mark for this part.

Quiz 1 is quite easy, most people score very high, so make sure you don't screw up. Quiz 2 is much more difficult, but people still score really well. Final is EXTREMELY HARD and CANNOT BE COMPARED to her quizzes. Her finals are only fill-in-the-blanks. She allowed us to bring a 2-sided A4 cheat sheet, but I honestly didn't even have to USE it. Her final is mostly on concepts, so don't only drill exercises, but make sure you get the concepts straight!!! I screwed up finals because I just did exercise without knowing the concepts well enough.

I got full mark for class participation, in-class exercise and quiz 1. But only got a few marks above mean for quiz 2 and finals. Still got B+ luckily.

Mainly covers the following financial statements and relevant knowledge:
1. Income Statement
2. Balance Sheet (Statement of Financial Position)

"Quizzes and final exam are all closed-book. Quiz 1 will cover all class sessions before Quiz 1. Quiz 2 will cover all sessions between Quiz 1 and Quiz 2. The final exam will cover everything we have discussed in the class."

sections.content:
I. Course Description

LSK 6066, email: [email removed], Tel. 2358 7582 Accessible via CANVAS
  Accounting is the language of business. In this course you will learn how to "speak" and "read" this new language. The course is designed to provide an overview of the financial accounting frameworks and processes leading to the preparation of financial statements, and develop your relevant skills to read, interpret and analyze corporate financial reports from various dynamic business perspectives.
II. Course Objectives
Upon the completion of this course, you should be able to:
1. Develop a comprehensive understanding and well-founded knowledge of financial accounting, covering:
a. the accounting categories: assets, liabilities, equity, revenues and expenses;
b. the ways an accounting system keeps track of data and information;
c. how generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) influence what is recorded in the books of an entity;
d. the preparation of a balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statement;
e. the reading, interpretation and analysis of a set of financial statements.
2. Understand the role of financial accounting in the decision-making process of business organizations, and apply financial accounting frameworks to business situations.
3. Form critical judgment covering an ability to identify and define accounting and business problems, apply analytical and quantitative techniques, and to make and justify decisions;
Page 1 of 5
4. Communicate effectively through collection, analysis and organization of information and ideas and their clear transmission;
5. Demonstrate teamwork, independence and creativity including working, learning and problem solving as a team and independently; and
6. Develop ethical and social understanding including a knowledge and respect of ethics and ethical standards in accounting and an understanding of social and civic responsibility.

sections.teaching:
Kelvin is the nicest professor -- he is always willing to answer questions during class and office hours, offers extra tutorials Saturday if students need extra help and is very approachable. However, he sometimes is not clear with his explanations and makes the content more confusing than it is. His classes were not very interesting, slides were similar to the textbook and are uploaded online, so overall you don't really need to go to class. However, he does give practice questions (you work on as a group in class and turn in before the end of class) during many classes which count towards your grade and help understand the material a lot more effectively than the lectures themselves.

So, I enjoyed how his class was structured into lecture and practice questions since he was very helpful in explaining HOW to do questions and the midterm and final short answer questions were very similar to practice questions.

If you are able to learn well on your own, then I would recommend Kelvin. If you need someone to explain concepts very clearly to you, I would not recommend his class.

sections.content:
I. Course Description
Accounting is the language of business. In this course you will learn how to "speak" and "read"
this new language. The course is designed to provide an overview of the financial accounting
frameworks and processes leading to the preparation of financial statements, and develop your
relevant skills to read, interpret and analyze corporate financial reports from various dynamic
business perspectives.
II. Course Objectives
Upon the completion of this course, you should be able to:
1. Develop a comprehensive understanding and well-founded knowledge of financial
accounting, covering:
a. the accounting categories: assets, liabilities, equity, revenues and expenses;
b. the ways an accounting system keeps track of data and information;
c. how generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) influence what is recorded
in the books of an entity;
d. the preparation of a balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statement;
e. the reading, interpretation and analysis of a set of financial statements.
2. Understand the role of financial accounting in the decision-making process of business
organizations, and apply financial accounting frameworks to business situations.
3. Form critical judgment covering an ability to identify and define accounting and business
problems, apply analytical and quantitative techniques, and to make and justify decisions;
Page 2 of 5
4. Communicate effectively through collection, analysis and organization of information and
ideas and their clear transmission;
5. Demonstrate teamwork, independence and creativity including working, learning and
problem solving as a team and independently; and
6. Develop ethical and social understanding including a knowledge and respect of ethics and
ethical standards in accounting and an understanding of social and civic responsibility.
III. Required Textbook
Libby, Libby, and Hodge. Financial Accounting, 9
th Edition (International Student Edition),
McGraw-Hill, 2017.
Note: You are required to purchase/get a copy of the textbook for your reading and practice of
the exercises/problems. Previous experience indicated that students who followed the reading
and practice in the teaching schedule were more likely to achieve a higher final grade.
IV. Course Assessment
Class Participation 10%
Quiz 1 10% (Sep 25 in class)
Mid-term Examination 25% (Oct 26 at 7:15-9:15pm, venue: TBA)
Quiz 2 15% (Nov 13 in class)
Final Examination 40%
Total: 100%
V. Course Policies
1. ACCT 2010 will have two class sessions per week that will each blend lecture, tutorial,
problem solving, and discussion together. Each topic will start with a lecture followed by a
discussion of some selected exercises/problems in class to improve your understanding of
and familiarity with the topic lectured, subject to availability of class time. I expect that you
will come to each class adequately prepared by a brief and first-time reading of the
appropriate chapter of the text. This allows you to pay more attention during a lecture to
issues that you have had difficulties in understanding the concepts and theories on your own.
The course is practical in nature and case-oriented requiring a problem-solving approach in
your learning and you are strongly encouraged to participate in doing the assigned
exercises/problems both inside and outside the class, though they are not collected and
graded. The solutions to all practice exercises/problems at the end of each chapter will be
posted on the course website after the chapter is done.
2. Class Participation. You are expected to attend all class regularly and on time, having
prepared beforehand all readings. I also expect you to be actively involved in all class
discussions, including asking questions, sharing your knowledge and experiences during
the class. All of us, your fellow students and me, will be benefited from insightful comments
and thought-provoking questions. On the contrary, those who chat in class are doing a
disservice to everyone present.
Page 3 of 5
3. Quizzes, Mid-term and Final Examinations. All quizzes/exams are closed book, closed
notes unless otherwise announced. The scope of the quizzes/exams will be announced
during class. Two quizzes held in class are scheduled on Mondays, September 25 and
November 13. An evening mid-term examination is scheduled on Wednesday, October
25, 2017 (7-9pm). The final examination is cumulative which may include topics under
the scope of the mid-term examination and quizzes. Programmable calculators are not
permitted.
It is expected that all students will take the quizzes and examinations at the scheduled time.
There will be NO make-up examination for the quizzes and mid-term. If absence from the
examination is due to unexpected medical emergency, the marks earned from the final
examination may be adjusted to substitute for the missing quizzes/mid-term grade. A
student foreseeing unavoidable absence due to a strong justification may seek approval from
the instructor for similar arrangement. Any other absent students will get zero marks for the
quizzes and mid-term exam.
4. Academic Honesty. It is important that students follow university regulations on academic
integrity and honesty. Academic dishonesty will not be tolerated and will be dealt with in
accordance with university rules, which can be accessed at the university website:
http://www.ust.hk/vpaao/integrity.
VI. Getting Help and Staying in Touch
I will post course-related information at the course web site on CANVAS. There are prescheduled
office consultation hours for the course. I suggest that you either visit during these
office consultation hours or make an appointment by sending an email to me. You can ask
substantive (as opposed to procedural) questions by e-mail — but please keep in mind that the
questions pertaining to the course material should be preferably asked in class.
Apart from asking questions in class, you can also use the discussion board on CANVAS to
raise smart questions for the benefit of everyone – the questioner, the instructor and other
students. I will check the discussion board and post replies regularly. You are encouraged to
reply to other students’ questions on CANVAS as part of a supportive learning environment.
I strongly encourage you to raise your questions either in class or on the discussion board as
soon as your problems arise. Do not allow your puzzles or confusions to accumulate because it
will be more difficult to solve them at a later stage.

sections.content:
Frankly speaking, if you have done well in the HKDSE, you have no excuse in failing this course.
First of all, this course is a general ledger-based course, implying that T-accounts AREN'T needed. Thus, if you excel in error correcting and above all, general journal, things would be easier.
Second, there aren't many new concepts. I can only recall the statement of cash flow, division of common stock and repurchase of common stock as new concepts.
Third, the answer is out there. Just don't make things complicated. This course resembles a simplified version of HKDSE, for example, when there is an estimation of allowance for doubtful debt, this course would ask you to Dr. bad debt Cr. allowance for doubtful debt. I have seen many classmates, including myself, of course, struggled to accept this fact. So my suggestion is--find the difference between this course and HKDSE and adapt to it. That's all.
sections.teaching:
Do not be deceived by this grading. I ain't suggesting that Kelvin is a mediocre instructor, or professor, whatever you like, despite I had seen his title as professor in his office.
He's passionate in teaching. There are a few examples supporting this statement.
1. Janitor on LSK's accounting department has applauded Kelvin as "an humble and amicable professor who is willing to answer anyone's question
2. I have witnessed him staying behind lectures and encompassed by a knot of students for at least an hour.
3. Well, this is on the record, which is he made extra classes on Saturday in LSK, despite the fact that I HAD NEVER attended any of those. Lel.
4. By the way, he focus on "conceptual understanding", which I don't give a **** coz here's the case: if you have studied BAFS, there isn't a need for you to understand A=S+L while if you haven't studied BAFS, may god bless you.
Lamentably, several examples disapproved the above statement.
1. His tone resembles your most boring teacher in secondary or primary school.
2. I have attended all his lectures and I have slept in quite a lot of them.
Here are some tips from me:
1. First, Kelvin speaks English fluently, in my opinion. But, according to my observation, he loves to say "in other words". So, if you find him not saying this, this maybe an impostor. Lel.
2. Second, Kelvin asked us to "pick up the convention" in doing general journals. In other words, follow his order and pick up the convention by writing narratives.
3. Third, there are in-class activities. Those exercises are EXTREMELY simple if you, again, do well in HKDSE's BAFS. So, here's the tip, if you have never got your ass on BAFS, it's my advice to find partners who have BAFS background. But, according to my experience, if you find this difficult, it's either your problem or doomsday of HKUST SBM.
4. Last but not least, well, I am more than certain that I didn't abuse the phrase "last but not least" cause I believe this is really the most crucial. FIND A COMPANY WHO IS HUMOROUS!!! This is really crucial because attending his lectures, given that you excel in secondary's BAFS, would bring you endless sleeps. You need a humorous, or pretty, either of them or both, classmate to keep you awake.
That's all for his teaching part.
sections.grading:
Frankly speaking, I have forgotten the distribution of percentage of different assessments.
Again, do not be deceived by the grading.
But I would say this course's transparency is an abomination.
Ok, let's go through the four assessments first.
1. in-class participation
2. mid-term
3. case study of ethics study
4. final
So, let me go through the tips briefly,
1. Again, those in-class exercises are nothing except jokes.
They are extremely easy, implying that you limit of score should ALWAYS be tending to 10, which is the maximum score.
2. Again, the mid-term inherited the simplicity.
I would say the SD is rather small, 10 out of 70. IDK
Kelvin loves to assess his students by MC
So, be careful
Long questions aren't the main character
Thus, focus on conceptual understanding.
3. Case study is an abomination.
First, the grades aren't disclosed.
Second, it's difficult
therefore, no tips at all
4. Again, the final is about simplicity again
It resembles part A of HKDSE's BAFS.
That's all
I scored A-
A bit sad, tho

Notes will be uploaded to canvas. Some concepts or points will not be written in the notes, but they will be tests in exams. There is a question in the final, "using the example that I explained in the class to illustrate...(9marks)" so for those who does not attend the class will GG. So better to attend the class.

ASSIGNMENT(5%)
You need to hand in your homework every week for the chapter she taught last week. She would give you a list of exercises and you need to choose at least three of them every time.

PARTICIPATION(5%)
You need to raise your hand to answer questions in the class or you can answer and ask questions on the Canvas discussion board. sections.content: The course cover basic accounting principle, including the four financial statements, journal entry and ledgers. Then the course focus on different items on those statements, namely Sales Revenue, Receivables, and Cash; Cost of Goods Sold and Inventory; Property, Plant, and Equipment; Intangibles; and Natural Resources; Liabilities; Bond Securities. Finally the course focus on Stockholders’ Equity, Statement of Cash Flows, and Analyzing Financial Statements, basically just calculating ratios and write short paragraph.
sections.teaching: The instructor is a new professor just graduated this year, so I can feel her passion in teaching. She taught in a way that is easy to understand without talking much unrelated stuff, her teaching is really about the accounting content of the course. I have no accounting background in secondary school, so I will say she really taught great.
sections.grading:
Participation 5%
After-class Practice Problems 5%
Quiz 1 15%
Quiz 2 15%
Final exam 60%

For participation, she said if she remember your face then you can get full credit.
After-class Practice Problems is essentially one assignment per week, for each assignment, the accuracy is not counted, so if you hand in all assignments, you get full credit.
For Quiz 1, I get 100/100. Mean: 86;  Median: 89; SD: 10
For Quiz 2, I get 95/100. Mean: 79;  Median: 81; SD: 14
For final, I get 113/120. Mean: 88;  Median: 92; SD: 15.
Finally got an A+.
As far as I know, a score slightly lower than 90% still give you an A, so I will say the grading is quite generous given the high mean.
sections.workload: Workload is fair. Two midterm and one final. Midterm is noncumulative while final cover all materials. You really need some exercise to familiarize yourself with the topic for good result. The required workload is basically the assignment each week, but I will say it is very light as she upload the solution along with the assignment which allow us just to copy the answer. The class content seems to be narrower than other professors. He teaches the content quiet slowly and have cut some syllabus.

The content of this course is more conceptual than the DSE BAFS accounting module. There are some difference on accounting treatments between DSE and ACCT2010 course. But Who had accounting background should catch up easily. While who don't have the background should spend more time to understand the concept and accounting procedures.

The professor teaches the concept quiet clearly and patiently. He could always provides interesting examples for explaining accounting concepts, but his tone is somehow boring.

He is also willing to share his advice and experience in accounting industry to students after classes. Who are passionate on accountancy may get interesting insight from him.
sections.grading:
Class activities and participation 10%
Case about professional ethics 15%
Mid-term exam 25%
Final exam(50%)

Try to be more active in his classes, he could really recognize students faces and their participation in his classes.

sections.content: Thoroughly covered course materials and basics of accounting. In the end students can expect to understand what accounting is, how it works, and international differences. Overall, content is very solid.
sections.teaching: Poor instruction, relies heavily on work outside class, and expectations not always clear. Not enough emphasis given to IFRS compared to its frequency on exams. Exams are disproportionately hard to classwork. Professor Shieh is humorous and has fun during class, but gets carried away and very often does not finish his lectures. He holds students past the end of class almost every lecture, and is arbitrarily serious during quizzes, making them unnecessarily difficult and confusing.
sections.grading: Tells students to expect new materials to show up on exams, even the final. Not inclined to give partial credit on questions, very difficult curve on exams. However, lowest quiz is dropped, which is helpful because everyone does poorly. A big problem is that the wording used on quizzes and exams is not clear, and clarification takes time away from the alotted time for evaluation.
sections.workload: Not demanding by itself, but to receive a good grade you must do all of the textbook practice problems. No homework, just review, reading, and practice outside class. In-class group assignments are good way to put together efforts to solve accounting tasks together and they raise your grade.

sections.content: Nothing too difficult, as it's just an introduction to financial accounting. This course covers material such as cash flow statements, income statements, the time value of money, depreciation, ratios, etc.
sections.teaching:
7/10

Your experience would greatly depend on whether you have learnt accounting before or not. If you have, be prepared to get bored out of your mind. He covers the content at a snail's pace. For instance, he talked about the concept of separate entity for about 40 minutes. Let that sink in. However, to the uninitiated, the professor would be incredibly good, since it is quite impossible to fall behind.

He is very casual and relaxed. He also uses good examples to illustrate his points.
sections.grading:
10/10

Pretty straightforward, with one midterm, one final, some class participation and the ethics case study (see Workload section of this review). Not too difficult to get an A. I myself have gotten an A+ with minimal background in accounting.
sections.workload:
10/10

The only homework in this course is an ethics case study, which is actually incredibly easy, since we are told to refer to the code of ethics for accountants.

sections.content: The class was not too difficult. I enjoy the subject of accounting more than other people though. The topics were introduced in an order that built off each other so it is good to attend class and keep up with the work.

sections.content: Throughout my 12 years of pre-university education, I've never learnt any accounting knowledge... And I regret that. As expected, I started off the course panicking, uncertain of what's to come. But the materials were way to understand and guides you to LITERALLY, learn the principles of accounting. To me, that's awesome. The only downside to the materials is our professor requires us to finish 12 chapters for the final exam, while other professors only need their students to go through 3-4 chapters for the exam. Believe me, that kinda sucks. But overall, I'd say I actually learnt something.
sections.teaching: Same with the title: meh. I mean, I'd say this course is a total disaster based on the extra chapters we need to study, but after attending all the lectures, I could still vaguely understand what she's talking about, even though getting good grades is another completely different matter. Her classes aren't that funny and energetic, but also wasn't too boring or dull. So I'd say her teaching was so so. See what I did there? :)
sections.grading: Not sure if I've been through hell in other courses or what, I actually think The grades in this course is amazing. I've seen other comments complaining about the harsh grading of this professor, and at first I had the same thought. My midterms were getting worst, and I only studied for three days for the final exam. Seemed like a B or B- to me. Shockingly, it's a B+. Yeah o know, it's not worth bragging, but still, that's awesome to me. Bad thing is till this day I still have no idea of the grade I got in the exam.
sections.workload: There's a shit ton of workload in this course, so get ready for some ass-whipping. Three quizzes(identical to midterms), one project and one exam. Sounds pretty normal, but it's complete shit compared to other professors. Started the project two days before it was handed in, had two free-rider groupmates, and I'm glad I grabbed it in on time. Again, till this date, I have no knowledge of my grades or whatsoever.

sections.content:
ACCT2010 covers some of the fundamental accounting principles. Possessing BAFS Background in HKDSE is a very big advantage because 80% of the course is quite similar what students learnt in senior secondary age.

For those who haven't studied accounting before (like me). Be prepared to pay effort to catch up. You have to learn 2-year stuff within 3 months.

But anyway I do not recommend anyone to give up from studying this course: It is very important that you need to know how to read financial statements  and pay attention to some ratios in preparing business case analyses (Case Competition, LABU stuff) or let say, ACCT2200 you will study in second year in HKUST.

Your hard work may not give you A in this course but the effort you pay can be turned into real outcomes in no longer future.
sections.teaching:
In general, her teaching is fair.

She teaches the concepts in a step-by-step manner. It can be boring to BAFS Students but it helps students with no accounting background to develop their concepts in a steady pace.

However, Professor Chen usually 'get lost' amid her teaching - and advanced concepts will be suddenly mentioned at the beginning of the semester. It is very hard for students with no accounting background to catch-up

The conclusion is: She hopes to develop concepts for students with no accounting background but in reality she kind of fails to do so. If you are students with BAFS experience, skip her class. If you are students without accounting background, attend her class, work harder, and you will be surviving then.
sections.grading:
Professor Chen offers some of the best grades in ACCT2010 (Li Xi is slightly better). Mean should be around B (or slightly lower)

The two mid-term are very very very important. Try your best to avoid any careless mistakes. Careless mistakes put you 5-10 marks lower (which is a deduction of 1-2% in total course score).

You need to get 0.8 - 1 SD higher than mean CONSTANTLY in ALL assessments to get A-range, I guess.

For your reference:
In-class Exercise (8 in total, 24%): 24/24
Quiz 1 (10%): 100/100 (Mean: 90, SD: 10)
Quiz 2 (20%): 86.5/100 (Mean: 82.4)
Final (super difficult and cumulative, 40%): 146.5/235 (~ +0.8 SD)
Participation: 6/6

My grade: B+

I am quite disappointed that I have worked super hard for this course (I almost gave up my MATH1003 for ACCT2010). However, when I compare with students who haven't studied accounting before and those in other classes (such as Tony, Kelvin Mak Class), what can I complain about? HaHa !!!!!!

sections.content: The content of the class very closely follows the four basic financial statements which are: Income Statement, Statement of Cash Flows, Balance Sheet, and Statement of Stockholder's Equity. Going into this class, I didn't have much excitement surrounding learning accounting, but I think that Professor Shieh did a great job of making what he had to teach quite exciting. Although the class had some of the hardest and most dense content of my semester, Tony broke it down nicely and the final ended up being one my easier ones.
sections.teaching:
As stated before, I think that Professor Shieh was a wonderful teacher. He frequently gave real world examples to ground the concepts. He also tried to be extra enthusiastic about what he was teaching in order to bring the overall energy of the course up as well.

I think that having a good professor for this class is important. I can only imagine how bored I would have been if my professor was not enthusiastic about what he/she was teaching.
sections.grading: Grading follows the regular SBM curve. Final is non-cumulative and also had a much higher curve than the midterm. There are quizzes, the lowest score of these is dropped. Definitely recommend studying quite hard for the first one.
sections.workload: This really depends on how much you care about your grade in this class. It is recommended that you go through each problem in the textbook if you want an A. This is what I did. However, problem is, many of these problems require you to write out entire financial statements which can take up to 2 pages back to back of writing. Ultimately tho, it might be the only way to commit such lengthy processes to memory well enough to do well on the exams.

sections.content:
The content is fairly straightforward, lecture slides and the textbook are easy to understand for the most part. The course introduces what financial accounting is and how its done. The topics covered were:
Balance Sheet, Income Statement, Statement of Stockholders Equity, Statement of Cash Flows, US GAAP vs IFRS, Journal entries and T-accounts, Adjusting entries, Reporting sales revenue, reporting cost of goods sold, reporting liabilities, reporting assets, reporting bonds and reporting owners equity.
sections.teaching: The professor was very engaging during class, and she taught the concepts clearly so that all the students were able to understand everything. She would also incorporate the use of in-class assignments and examples from the textbook to demonstrate the concepts taught in the class.
sections.grading:
In my opinion, the grading for this course was alright.
3 mini exams (each on 3 chapters) - 13% each
Final exam (cumulative) - 40%
Participation - 5%
Group case assignment - 6%
In-class assignments - 10%
sections.workload: The main workload were the mini exams, because there was one almost every month. There were homework assignments but they were not mandatory, it was just to help for exam prep. You're given a long time to complete the case assignment so it's not very time-consuming.

REMEMBER TO ATTEND MOST OF THE LESSONS EVEN THOUGH YOU CAN LEARN IT AT HOME!!!!!

sections.teaching: Kinda boring and the pace is a little bit slow for those who have learnt before, but it is VERY FAST and hard to pick up for those who have not learnt before.
sections.grading:
Normal
but the midterm and final are very difficult.
sections.workload:
The workload is little, there is only one essay-type assignment (which is a little complicated as you will have to read some resources).
The overall workload is little comparing with other accounting instructors.

sections.content: Similar to DSE BAFS (accounting module), some new topics( eg,statement of cash flows). However, midterm and final quite difficult. If you pay effort, you will get a good result, (even though you have never studied acct in secondary school before).
sections.teaching:
Quite interesting, good professor with clear presentation skills
Teach with Powerpoint slides, not boring at all

sections.content: The content is more or less the same as what you have learnt in secondary school in the first few lessons but you will find something new in the following lessons such as shipping term and statement of cash flow.  The powerpoint is simple and clear.
sections.teaching: He taught students with real daily examples and sometimes ask questions. His lesson is interesting.
sections.grading: He will count your attendance by asking questions and mark down on his logbook if you have answered.
sections.workload: He only give us one case study as assignment.

Attendance and Participation 5%

In-class Group Exercises 10%

sections.grading: Normal
sections.workload: 會分組做grp exercise，然後每grp佢會影張相，所以佢認得哂大部分人。而grp exercise方面有6個，每個10分，全部都係手板眼見功夫，基本上之前嗰堂有聽書都會識做兼滿分，不過分組最好搵啲有讀過acct嘅人咁就輕鬆得多啦。

sections.content: The content was above average. The professor followed the textbook in an orderly manner with high relevancy with the textbook in regards to text. She also lectured with powerpoints during class and shared them online as well.
sections.teaching: Her teaching was very organized and well-prepared. She will have certain patterns to lead her class.
sections.grading: I got a C from this course, which was pretty predictable. This is a pretty rigorous course and participation matters.
sections.workload: There was a monthly test for every three chapters. I think it's best to read each chapter of the textbook before class to excel in this class.

sections.content: 這門課不算特別有意思，但是是解讀商業信息的基礎課所以還是比較重要的吧
sections.teaching: 教授上課喜歡講跟accounting本身不是很有關係但是有意思的商業小知識
sections.grading: 大家分數相差都不太大，所以小小分差可能給grade給的都會不太一樣..
sections.workload: 還好，沒有作業

sections.content:
It's about financial accounting which covers these chapters:
- 4 financial statements
- T-account
- Operating activities
- Bad debts
- Inventory & Cost of Goods Sold
- Depreciation
- Time value of money
- Bonds
sections.teaching: I only came to 3 or 4 classes so I cannot say much about his teaching, but he likes to give real life examples about the topics discussed in class.
sections.grading:
Super good grade. He gives the largest number of As compared to other ACCT 2010 professors.

Midterm : 45% (mean:88/100)
Final : 55% (mean:67/100)

You can also gain bonus point up to 4 points by presenting a business news in class or solving an exercise in class or being active in class.
sections.workload: No workload. Only midterm and final, and the exams are easy.

sections.content:
Content is not too heavy because it is non cumulative and therefore your midterm exam will cover 6-7 chapters and the final will cover the chapters not covered after that.

Content is quite tough for students who have not done accounting before.

The individual quizzes are quite straightforward as he will tell you exactly what topic to prepare for and the group quizzes are tough when you have freeloaders in your group however not too big of a deal because they are open book.
sections.teaching: Professor doesn't mind whether or not you attend class however it's pretty useful for the parts of the course that involve mathematics because he explains these well. Other parts of the course can be easily understood through the textbook and the professor isn't very helpful.
sections.grading:
Grading is based on
- In class participation (5%)
- 3 Individual Quizzes, best of 2 taken (10%)
- Group quizzes (10%)
- Midterm exam (35%)
- Final exam (40%)

Midterm exam is very difficult but then final is made much easier.
sections.workload:
The workload is not too heavy, he will suggest doing some background reading before the lesson which is actually quite helpful but of course not mandatory.

The quizzes are every 2-3 lessons and he alternates between group quiz and individual quizzes.

sections.content:
Content is less than other teachers
mostly theoretical for his class
no making of full balance sheet or income statement
sections.teaching:
he explains some points in his ppt but elaboration is sometimes confusing.
have to self-study for the basic accounting principles and skills
easier to understand if you already studied accounting before
sections.grading: His grading is fair, exams are based on examples in his ppt. participation marks are important to score a good grade in this course
sections.workload:
he gives class activities which students are supposed to do in class but he posts them on canvas already, so you can do it at home first
essay is an ethics case of no longer than 3 pages
no quiz

sections.teaching: Tony is a great professor but giving out fair grades :( He is passionate in teaching, answered all students' question clearly, you may take his course if you'd like to earn more participation marks.
sections.grading: Fair grade only, participation doesn't count much but do help. Final, mid-terms and quizzes take most, so you'd better work more on studying.
sections.workload: Workload acceptable, there were in-glass group exercises, quizzes, mid-terms and final exam. Unlike other professors, Tony's paper is comparatively harder, longer and no MCs. Might be killed by tricky question types.

sections.content: no attendance requirement. There are two simple midterms, but the final is extremely difficult. Cheatsheet is allowed in final.
sections.teaching: She uses examples to explain different cases. But the speed of explaining is a little bit slow. She will distribute her own notes and i think it is not bad.
sections.grading: I got a B+ by gaining 82% overall. You can gain participation mark by cleaning the blackboard or answering questions. Marks are included by handling in in-class exercises.
sections.workload: In class exercises are distributed every week and students need to hand them in every week. Those exercises are not that difficult since they are similar to the exercises in the book.

sections.content: The content taught was appropriate, throughout the semester 9 chapters were taught.
sections.teaching: Kelvin is a knowledgeable professor, he answered questions asked by students very patiently. Moreover, there are some practice questions that Kelvin will do with us during class. Kelvin stated his teaching with the final financial statements to consolidate the most basic elements of financial accounting.
sections.grading: The grading scale is appropriate, though the essay handed in was not returned in therms of score or feedback.
sections.workload: The workload of the course isn't very heavy, no group project throughout the whole semester but an individual assignment of 3 pages is required. Kelvin gave us enough sources and hints to complete the essay.

sections.content: Teaching syllabus is around 10 chapters, while other professors may only have 8 chapters, so it will be more difficult to get a higher grade.
sections.teaching: Good teaching as she will review all the examinations questions after examination and give us tips about the exams.
sections.grading: Overall the teaching is very good, but the grade is a little "broken".
sections.workload: Exam syllabus is a little bit too much, comparing with the other professors. There are three mid-terms but it is easier to catch up the content of ACCT. However, there are no homework but only class assignment.

sections.content: The course is quite similar to the DSE accounting syllabus
sections.teaching: Every class a class note would be given, you can download it from canvas. Also the prof. is really nice ,if you have any questions you can ask after class or on canvas discussion board
sections.grading:
Participation = 5%
In class exercise = 10%
Midterm = 30%
Final = 45%

The professor will remember your face and your name so just raise your hand and ask some questions to get full 5% marks.
sections.workload: Here's only in-class exercise around once a week,no project or other quiz. extra exercises are provided, you can do it for practices.

sections.content: A really good course if you wanna learn basic accounting. The content is pretty basic as it does not require you any previous knowledge of accounting to excel in the class.
sections.teaching: Tony's teaching is excellent in my opinion.
sections.grading:
The Grading Scheme is as the following:
Attendance and Participation 5%
In-class Group Exercises  10%
Three In-class Quizzes @ 20 points each (drop the lowest one) 10%
Mid-term Exam 35%
Final Examination (non-cumulative) 40%

Do well in the midterm and you'll do fine. Do ask questions in the class as he will remember your name. The group exercise will be for 3-4 students per group. There were 5 group exercises (he initially said there would be 6 but there wasnt enough time), so only 4 was taken. The quiz will be a bit trickier (even than the midterm and the final, lol) but it doesnt matter that much.
sections.workload: The workload of this course is relatively low. There is no project, just midterm, final, and some quizzes, and also in-class exercises. Remember to do exercises from the book.

sections.content: This course is suitable for students who want to learn basic accounting knowledge. Basic information like credit and debit,  different type of accounts, how to prepare income statement, statement of cash flow, balance sheet and how are they related, etc.
sections.teaching: Professor Li used powerpoint and in-class exercise to teach, around 30% of the lessons are taught about financial news, which is not very related to accounting but it was good to students who want to know more about operation of business companies.
sections.grading: 45% midterm exam; 55% final exam. The final exam was not cumulative but it was not stated clearly (better if he had stated this); he tried his best to give us marks (which is true) and graded normally.
sections.workload: Very light workload, no attendance is taken and no assignments. Only in-class questions were given and it contains no marks. You can get bonus marks in final exam if you do presentations or ask/answer questions during lesson.

sections.content: the course is quite similar to the DSE accounting syllabus
sections.teaching: every class a class note would be given, you can download it from canvas. Also the prof. is really nice ,if you have any questions you can ask after class or on canvas discussion board.
sections.grading: there are 6% attendance mark, you just need to answer one  question during the class for getting all 6% mark.
sections.workload: there's only in-class exercise around once a week,no project or other quiz. extra exercises are provided, you can do it for practices.

sections.content:
We learnt 12 units in this one term, all of which appeared in the final exam. We followed a textbook, which I recommend you getting a hard copy to. All topics we very relevant to accounting, but were very content heavy.
Chap1: Financial Statements and Business Decisions
Chap2: Investing and Financing Decisions and the Accounting System
Chap3: Operating Decisions and the Accounting System
Chap4: Adjustments, Financial Statements and the Quality of Earnings
Chap6: Reporting and Interpreting Sales Revenue, Receivables and Cash
Chap7: Reporting and Interpreting Cost of Goods Sold and Inventory
Chap8: Reporting and Interpreting Property, Plant, and Equipment; Intangibles; and Natural Resources
Chap9: Reporting and Interpreting Liabilities
Chap10: Reporting and Interpreting Bonds
Chap11: Reporting and Interpreting Owners' Equity
Chap13: Statement of Cash Flows
sections.teaching: Professor Ho was a good teacher in that she provided us many tips on how to calculate the different values we needed. She was always on topic and also gave us real life examples while teaching. I would only comment negatively on her organisation (in moving on from topic to topic) and technical skills, as there were many times I could not see what she was writing. Also, while she had her moments where she was engaging, due to how she speaks and its pace, it's very easy to get too comfortable... even when in her slow speeches she is going through the whole chapter in that one lesson.
sections.grading:
I GOT A C+ DESPITE BEING WITHIN STANDARD DEVIATION IN ALL EXAMS AND SIGNIFICANTLY ABOVE AVERAGE FOR ONE OF THEM. I DO NOT EVEN KNOW MY GRADE FROM THE FINAL AND IT SEEMS THAT I WILL NEVER KNOW.

In addition, I have cross checked with some of my friends' grades and it turns out they also got a C range! One of them even just got a C despite being above average for all mini exams! Just what????
sections.workload:
3 f'n mini exams, case study right after and then a final. In between, we also had 6 in-class assignments. Participation points are also given out like crazy, so you may end up being the only one in class without one if you do not constantly study for the lesson. Also, do not forget it is 12 units you are going through. Not 6 or 8 like the other classes. And you are tested on all of them!

The workload is not worth the grade.

ppt and  extra example
quite similar with the acct in secondary school
eg inventory, balance sheet, income statement etc.
jot down everything (as more as you can )in the lesson because they will appear in the exam
sections.teaching:
quite interesting
teaching  process slow
many Q&A session
over-run every lesson
there are some practices in the lesson (work in group)----->participation mark
sections.grading:
good
do not take attendance
it is easy to get good grade if you have studied BAFS

His class is interesting
Very suitable for the students whom haven't studied acct before
But try not to skip any lectures
sections.teaching:
He did help many fm who dont know acct before. He is patient and friendly.
He seldom skipped the topics like other prof. I found acct is quite interesting after his lectures.
sections.grading:
Below mean then u c+
Midterm below mean a little
Exam above mean a little
Grp ex is not good as well
finally B-
sections.workload:
Many quizzes and group ex.
Dont have a group with your classmates who haven't study acct.

sections.content: for the final exam, it is not cumulative so the workload is comparatively lower
sections.teaching: tony will use cantonese to answer students' questions and he maintained a good atmosphere in class. but sometimes it is a bit too fast and what he explained is too difficult
sections.grading: my score is slightly below mean in midterm and higher than mean a bit in the final. while my participation mark should be 0 and much lower than mean in those quizzes and in class group works and i still got an B
sections.workload: many in class group works. there are a lot of extra information in lesson so it is not recommended to skip lesson

sections.content: quite useful
sections.teaching: Not bad for classes and the powerpoint included most of the important concepts of the course
sections.grading: my marks of so called "mini examsss" ( I bet the reason why they dont call it midterm is that a term cant be mid for three times!!!!!) was overall above mean  (the marks of final is not released and the whole course vanish without a trace on canvas so as all the marks of project and quizzes, theres no way that you could argue with the professor about your grading as even if you ask for the marks and details of your grading no one will EVER reply you) and eventually I got a  C range!!!!!
sections.workload: we're required to finish ~6 in-class assignments and which means you hav to attend most of the lessons to keep yourself informed of the date when you will hav to finish all the in-class assignments and you will also hav 3 mini exams(which are actually midterms but they polished their names and patently they were never as MINI as they claimed) at the end of the term we hav to submit a critical thinking project, its not as shit as the above provided that your group mates are not free rider or retard that cant read the instructions!!!!!!!

sections.content: It is basic accounting knowledge which is not difficult for completely new learners. It mainly covers financial statement and some GAAP concepts,
sections.teaching: Professor is nice and prepared PPT well. Her teaching is average and easy to follow.
sections.grading:
3-4 mid-term, one final and one accounting case study (group format with maximum 4 people/group)
participation point would be given when you ask/answer professor question.

I guess the mean is B as many people I know got good result.
sections.workload: not heavy . one group project and some easy in-class assignments.

sections.content: 做為第一門ACCT課，內容很基礎，無非是基本概念和報表罷了。LI XI上課會有很多有意思的擴展，對於國際局勢啊金融市場啊評論也很有趣，個人覺得一學期下來收穫很多。
sections.teaching: LIXI教的比較淺（和課本難度持平），但是非常良心。NOTES、exercise全部課堂上會發打印版，簡直良心。概念解釋的還是很清楚的，對於完全沒接觸過的初學者而言完全沒有理解方面的問題。需要注意的是第一章導論部分LIXI會講的很細緻，初學會誤以為課很難，實際上學到後面會加深對於前面章節的理解，重複的內容很多。
sections.grading: LIXI自稱龜神，A range事全部2010裡最多。四個BONUS很好拿。
sections.workload: 一個midterm一個final四個bonus。bonus包括白板演示做題、新聞pre（年稿即可）和participate。workload在各pro之間比較算很小的。不過初學ACCT需要多花時間在自己理解概念上。LIXI的in-class exercise實際上是midterm和final的同類型題，課下多做課本練習也很有用。

sections.content: Not so difficult to understand.
sections.teaching:
Able and very pleased to answer students' questions.
Well teaching
He explained the concept clearly and easy for students to understand.
There are many foreigners in the class and they usually ask a lot of questions and that also help other students to understand the concepts.
sections.grading: not so good in mid-term but got the highest in the fianl, at last get a A+
sections.workload:
No HW
3 in class quiz and count the best two
3 to 4 in-class group exercise and there will be hints and instruction
1 mid-term and 1 final

sections.content: Basic accounting stuff, mostly dse bafs content
sections.teaching: good professor, easy to understand. Although I did not take bafs in dse i can still fully understand the concept.
sections.grading:
Attendance and Participation 5
In-class Group Exercises 10
Three In-class Quizzes @ 20 points each (drop the lowest one) 10
Mid-term Exam 35
Final Examination (non-cumulative) 40
sections.workload: he has given all end of chapter ex solution to us, and it is optional. The only real wordload is mid term and final. grp ex and quiz are easy as long as u attend all lessons and understand the concepts:)

sections.content:
The course includes 11 chapters.
It nearly covers the whole syllabus taught in NSS
Excluding partnership and some accounting principles.
But something new are the calculation on bonds and fixed assets.
And some terms used in American accounting are quite different from which in British accounting.
So even though you have learnt accounting at high school
This course can still be difficult to you.
ESPECIALLY BONDS!!! BONDS!!! BONDS!!!

But honestly, the material taught is quite comprehensive and useful.
At least, the curriculum is good.
sections.teaching:
Though her notes are quite clear and easy to understand.
But the teaching routine was FUCKING MESSY!!!
She always skipped to another example without any omens
Even the geniuses like Gbus students could not catch up with what she was saying.
Besides that, some of the calculation methods she taught are different with which in textbook.
It is difficult for you to do self-revision!!!

But because of the well-prepared notes,
She might be a good instructor to those beginners.

Btw, when you ask her question,
Her response was usually VERY VERY VERY unclear.
But honestly she is nice and willing to answer any questions.
sections.grading:
Participation 6%
In-class exercise 24%
Quiz 1 10%
Quiz 2 20%
Final Exam 40%

The quizzes were extremely easy even a junior secondary student can get a pass
So she expects you guys will get full marks

But if you make few careless mistakes just like what I did
It is nearly impossible for you to get a range

Because the final exam was FUCKING DIFFICULT!!!
The question is as long as a comprehension
Even though she allow you to bring a cheat sheet
It is USELESS for this exam!!!
And mostly you can't even get partial credits
Even I have got 5* in DSE, I just got nearly 60% of marks.
And finally just a B+
Overall I got 82.38%
sections.workload:
The in-class exercises are easy
And mostly you can just copy the answer she posted in canvas
(( It is sure that I do not suggest you copy answers....

But the deadline she set is fucking not reasonable!!!

sections.content:
Quite similar to DSE BAFS (accounting).
Topics like Cash flow, bad debts and bonds are more challenging than the DSE syllabus
sections.teaching: It is sometimes hard to follow during lectures, but prof is patient and willing to answer questions after class. She replies to canvas discussion questions quickly and clearly.
sections.grading:
- 2 Quizzes (midterms) : very easy (most people get full marks)
- Final exam: very very difficult (highest score 174/235)
- 8 in-class exercises
- class participation: cleaning the board/ answering question
marks for in-class exercises, class participation are easy to get
the two quizzes are very simple (for people who have not studied accounting in high school as well)
grades are quite good
sections.workload:
Besides midterm exams and final exam, all you have to do is hand in at least 8 in-class exercises, which are quite easy and short.
You just have to try your best to complete it, but don't have to get 100% correct for full credit.

sections.content:
Useful
Mainly from the textbook though she does try to add little background knowledge of her own
11 Chapters in total
Most questions mainly come from the textbook
so its better to revise that
sections.teaching:
Very BAD
Not due to a lack of effort
Her lessons are very chaotic and not structured at all
Nearly everyone has no idea what she is talking about
She jumps from one example to another without even telling us that she is
sections.grading:
24% is in-class exercises which you don't have to even do but still I only did half :(
Though there is no class participation these exercises are in fact ur class participation marks
For the two mid  terms they are too easy
But the final will make u pray to God even u don't believe him
It is the most difficult exam I ever did in my life
sections.workload:
In hindsight
Even though it seems u don't have to put in a lot of effort when u are doing in class exercises actually for the final u have to put it in a lot of effort that it seems

sections.content: The course only covered some of the most basic accounting principal. If you are going to take accounting as your major, I wouldn't recommend this course, but if you take it only because its pre-enrolled you MUST be in this class.
sections.teaching: He teaches every material very clearly and he make sure everyone in the class understand the materials.
sections.grading: Grading is good, but its a little bit unfair because  students who have learned accounting in high school are also in this class, so it will be a little bit tougher to catch up for those who haven't learnt accounting before.
sections.workload: No compulsory assignment but to do well in exam we have to do the in class exercises and practice questions recommended by the instructor

sections.content: This course is mainly about basic accounting knowledge. The content is not easy to understand for some people who had never learned accounting, but hard works pay off. For people who know those basic things, it is very easy for them to get a good grade.
sections.teaching: Tony is a good teacher in terms of solving students' questions about accounting. It is not uncommon to find out that a lot of lecture time are spent on answering questions. But sometimes he might spend so many time on it, and may slow down the schedule and make the schedule tight.
sections.grading: As accounting is really a course with exact answers and the content of this course is basic, the mean if the quiz or exam are usually quit high. For Tony, the number of a range are not so high and usually the mean is B-/C+.
sections.workload: There is only one midterm, compared to other tutors for this course. In class group exercise and quiz are also required. However, the questions are quit difficult and tricky. Students may need to spend lots of time on practicing.

sections.content:
It would be quite challenging for students haven't studied accounting before. (One chapter for two lectures)
Mid terms are quite easy but final is difficult.
sections.teaching: A nice teacher. She is willing to explain once again if you don't understand. You can ask her during the lecture/after the class/on canvas.
sections.grading: Some people who are below mean can still get a B+. You can get a A if you are above one SD.
sections.workload:
In class exercise

sections.content: Basics of financial accounting: accounting system, 4 basic financial statements, and the accounting treatments for the items which appear on the statements, like revenue, inventory, long-term assets, liabilities/bonds, cash flow, etc.
sections.teaching:
Prof Chen's lecture notes are precise and clear, though having typos and calculation mistakes sometimes. Proof-reading is essential for her LOL.
However, she uses examples not stated in the lecture notes to illustrate the concepts very often. That's fine for me as a previous BAFS student in high school, but certainly not okay for my peers without accounting background.
Nevertheless, I must say Prof Chen is a nice professor. She is always patient to answer the questions raised by my peers with a smile. She also treats every single word she says seriously. One day she shared a piece of information about the characteristics of the accounting frauds. On the next day I saw her announcement on Canvas, asking us not to use race and gender to judge others (Although I think no one treat her words seriously...). That's really hard to find a professor treating teaching seriously as her.
sections.grading:
Grading scheme:
24% In-class exercises
6% Class participation
10% Quiz 1
Mean: 90/100  SD: 10
(Just because it is extremely easy.)
20% Quiz 2
Mean: 82/100  SD: 12
(The level of difficulty is moderate.)
40% Final Exam
Mean: 126/235  SD: 26
(Testing your ability to apply the concepts in the real business world. Very challenging.)

Got full marks for Quiz 1, in-class exercises and class participation. 98 marks for Quiz 2 and 156/235 for final exam. Getting approximately 1 SD above mean can secure an A, and I think the grading is very generous.
sections.workload: Absolutely acceptable. One in-class exercise for each 2-3 lessons, after a chapter was finished. You have to hand in at least 8 in-class exercises out of 11 in the whole semester. Prof Chen also encourages us to do more exercises on the textbook, but not compulsory.

sections.grading: Grading is generally very fair, but it's hard to cross the gap between a B and an A. The midterm average was around a 60 and the final average was around a 70. I found the final to be much easier than the midterm, which was extremely difficult.

sections.content: The content covered in the first few lessons is quite similar to those DSE students learnt in high school according to my friends. Nonetheless there were many new concepts. Be aware of what Prof. Tony says during class about the concepts.
sections.teaching: Prof. Tony is a very passionate teacher. He takes the time explain concepts so make sure to take notes. However, don't forget to practice the textbook questions a lot because those are ultimately what will be tested in the exam. I liked his class because he was funny and interactive. He often asked people questions and took the effort to remember our names. He did mention that he cares a lot about,  impression during his grading so it may be good for people who often speak up in class.
sections.grading: Although the class was interesting, its quite difficult to stay on top of everyone in order to get a good grade as many people have learnt accounting before in high school. You have to work extra hard from the beginning because the mean was quite high. He also has a lot of quizzes and in class exercises. Make sure to find the right group unless you are confident that you will get everything correct.
sections.workload: There was no compulsory homework but you are basically recommended to practice regularly after each chapter. You will struggle if you do not practice regularly. There are also quizzes and in class assignments (group and used to take attendance) so you have to be prepared after each chapter. There was one mid term and one final exam (non cumulative).

i find it useful
sections.teaching:
Prof was emphasizing on the basic, Debit Credit. So, it would be easier for you learning the next chapters. He went super fast on the following chapters though. Listen to him carefully because he emphasizes on particular things that will come out at the exams,.

Prof is very open to questions and he's nice. He also relates the syllabus to the worldwide news and everyday life.
If you ever learned accounting before then he's right for you. But if you haven't then ... you will find it a bit hard to catch what he's saying.
sections.grading:
The grading is pretty generous but you have to be  extremely careful in doing the midterm and final.
No attendance
Midterm : 45%
Final      : 55%
Midterm was easy, so it really helps you.  Lots of textbook-ish questions appeared in midterm. Make sure that you come to the midterm. If not, your final would be 100% your grade.

Final was a lot harder. No more questions similar to textbook qs. Prof took it to another new level, new forms of questions. You really must understand the whole concept. I took accounting on secondary so it wasn't that bad.

You can gain extra 4 bonus points by actively asking & answering questions, solving the problem on the stage, and bringing financial news to the class.

I got 98 on midterm, 95 on final and 2 extra points and finally got an A+.

Moreover, it sometimes make students like me feel bored.
sections.grading: I perform fine with this course and getting scores above mean in the course, and I get a B+ for this.This is a fine grade for me so I don't have much to complain. sections.content: Beginner level. The course starts to get difficult only at the very last few lectures. Very easy to follow in general.
sections.teaching: Teaching is excellent. Power points are very clear and straight forward. You have to pay attention in class to fill the blanks though, but the class is good enough to pay attention. The Prof. jokes a lot and guides students to arrive at the correct answers; he provides extra useful tips occasionally.
sections.grading: The bad thing about the course is that many students with prior knowledge of accounting is registered into the same class with people who don't. The grading is thus very extreme. However, comparing to other profs of the same course, Prof. Hsu's "mid-terms" (mini-exams actually) and final exam are the easiest.
sections.workload: Very light workload. The only assignments are 2-3 group assignments of real life cases; they are very easy to score above 90%. Mini-exams (3 in total if my memory does not fail me) are easy enough to score 95% or above; the mean and sd are very high though. The Final exam are more difficult than the mini-exams, but manageable. There are classwork every class, but the amount is minimal. He  counts your attendance (makes a seating plan and checks accordingly), and allows 2 unexplained absence.

sections.content: The class contains nearly every aspect in financial accounting expect several complicated issues which will be covered in the Intermediate Accounting. Among the four financial statements, three of them will be covered in exams and the remainder, the Statement of Shareholders' Equity will be reference only.
sections.teaching: Generally, Prof Shieh's lecture is very clear and easy to comprehend with lot's of interesting stories about accounting and business. One of my favourites is the Arthur Anderson fraud, which he mentioned a lot. Besides, he is really a nice person whom you can chat with during the office hour and ask any academic stuff. But, it seemed like Prof. Shieh assumed that everyone in the class was already familiar with accounting so at the beginning a lot of guys like me who hadn't learnt accounting before got totally puzzled.
sections.grading:
Here comes the awful part. The syllabus stated the grading will be accorded to:
Participation: 5%
In-class exercises: 10%(Drop the lowest one)
Quizzes: 10%(Drop the lowest one)
Midterm exam: 35%
Final exam: 40%
From the information above, you may see that the midterm exam bears the same importance as the final. Yup you're right. I did horribly in the exam(below mean) but got nearly full mark in the final. BUT! THERE IS NO USE AT ALL!  
So, apparently, don't fail any of the exam.
sections.workload: The instructor will present the recommended homework in the book but no homework will be checked. But, the best strategy is always, the more the better.

sections.content:
基本上account都係果啲野，中學讀過bafs就應該幾輕鬆，一半以上都係中學學既野(a/c module)，dep、allowance、格式之類既野會有啲唔同，仲有唔少新野，不過好快上手，例如：Statement of Cash Flow / Stockholders' Equity等等。
佢唔cover到ratio，冇乜野要背，基本上有上堂再做啲數就好輕鬆。

Topic (通常兩堂教一個)
Ch.1 Overview of corporate financial reporting
Ch.2 Transaction analysis and the balance sheet
Ch.3 Revenue and expense recognition and the income statement
Ch.4 Adjustments, financial statements, and the closing process
Ch.6 Sales revenue and receivables
Ch.7 Cost of goods sold and inventory
Ch.8 Plant assets and intangibles
Ch.9 Reporting and interpreting liabilities
Ch.10 Bonds and long-term debts
Ch.11 Owners' equity
Ch.12 Statement of cash flows

啲in-class ex好有幫助，等於同你review果日教d咩，到時考試就好輕鬆，所以記得一定要上堂。

上堂冇得用電腦、電話，記得一定要PRINT NOTES，一黎佢規定要，二黎好多野係佢份ppt先有，Canvas果份冇，要自己抄返低。

讀過acct都知，書除咗做ex就冇乜用，佢notes好清晰，唔會好似某啲prof咁成版都係字，有唔少公仔同圖表幫你理解同溫習，好方便。

冇讀過bafs既都可以放心，因為prof成日都話可以忘記哂中學啲野，而且佢都教得幾詳細、幾易明，最緊要明最基本既concept，唔明既可以透過in-class ex幫手，再唔係可以落堂問佢問題，就算係佢教既以外既野佢都會答，份人好NICE。

唔好走堂，記得帶NOTES就得。

sections.content:
I would describe this as an extension of the financial accounting in the BAFS syllabus, those with accounting background will have an edge over those without in general.
However, even though some basic principles like double entry is the same, the format of various financial statements will be quite different from the DSE format.
The exercises he provided is from the book, and the answer key will also be provided, so I find the textbook quite redundant and expensive... But it will be useful if you know nothing about accounting or you cannot understand a word during his lessons.  
My advice is if you learnt them in the past, you may skip some lectures, but if you haven't, you better attend the lecture and try hard to understand his teaching.

Fair to Good grading.
For your reference, this is my mark for obtaining an A+:
Final Exam (100/115)
Mid-term (108/110)
I have asked a few of my friends, I found he gave quite a number of A and A+, even if you are in B range, he tends to give B+ instead of B or B-.
Please be noted that, there will be past paper available online, but you have to find that out by yourself... And the exam is generally difficult than the exercises (quite difficult indeed...)

sections.content: The content is relatively comprehensive. There is almost nothing in the book that isn't extensively covered in class. Whatever is taught is generally on the examinations too.

Dr. Chen is pretty monotone but she's thorough. She'll go through whatever is necessary and omit things that are not relevant to examinations. She'll give "good to knows" and will explicitly point out exactly what you need to know. So pay attention to those. If you follow carefully, you'll have no problems with the mid terms plus exams.

She likes participation, so participate as much as possible.
sections.grading:
Grading is lenient. and participation plays a big role for grabbing back marks that you lost during the assignments.
However! It may be different for you, but the final has an absolutely different format from your mid-terms and in class exercises. For you to get a good grade in the final, you legitimately need to know how to read balance sheets and financial statements. So you need to revise that carefully.
sections.workload:
Workload is pretty light. There are 5 assignments. The worst out of the 5 will be omitted for marking. The rest are in class assignments that are done at the end of classes. There are no other homework assignments so the rest is on you in terms of studying.

Good luck.

sections.content: Financial accounting was relatively easy. I did not take accounting in my highschool, so I did not have any knowledge before. However, the content was really simple and easy to understand.
sections.teaching: He is  a really good teacher. Explains everything really well. Makes the class really personal and answers any questions you may have. No electronic equipments allowed. So will need to bring a hard copy of the content to every class.
sections.grading: Grading quite tough
sections.workload: Workload was relatively low. Had 3 small quizzes, 2 assignments, and 1 final exam. Have to work with partner.

sections.content:
The professor covered the first 11 chapters in the textbook except chapter 4.
She gave adequate examples to illustrate the concepts and raised tricky questions for us to think. She will cover what she has mentioned as well as sample paper in the exam.
sections.teaching:
Logic teaching and many examples.

She is always willing to answer questions and make appointment with students.

very helpful and friendly
sections.grading: Though the final was too difficult, I think, the professor tried to give as much a range as possible. (at least she said so...)
sections.workload:
fair workload.
In-class exercise
no homework
need to do exercise yourself

sections.content: It is a rather elementary course is about fundamental knowledge of accounting: double entry, journal, financial statements etc. For those who have studied BAFS in DSE should have a bit advantage over the others, but it is suggested to attend classes or practice on the given questions in textbook as some contents covered in DSE were said to be insufficient.
sections.teaching: Professor was nice and willing to answer questions.
sections.grading: Grading of this course is quite fair: it actually reflects how much effort you devoted into studying. Even an ameteur in accounting can score higher marks than those studied BAFS before if they worked hard enough.
sections.workload: As I said before this course requires hardwork, but its workload is still manageable.

sections.content: Basic things in accounting that you have to know. Contents are simple and straight-forward
sections.teaching: She taught pretty well, but you need to self-study some of the topics to catch up in class if this is your first time studying accounting.
sections.grading: If you studied and prepared well before the exams and achieve above mean scores, you will pretty easily get B or B+ since professor usually gives out full marks for homework. Cheat sheet can be a great help during exams but don't cram too many things in there because you might spend all your time during exam looking for the stuff you have written.
sections.workload:
Not much work given out. All you need to do is finish 6 homework with your group.
Midterm exams were not that tough. The professor tells you what kind of questions she will ask before the exams and goes through questions that your having difficulties with. She also allows students to bring in a double-sided cheat sheet with them and it could be a great help.
Final exam was a bit tough, and there aren't much time to look through 3 double-sided cheat sheets so better prepare well beforehand.

sections.content:
The fundamental knowledge of financial accounting, such as journal entry, T-accounts and financial statements.

Accounting standard used: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

Students who had studied accounting before (such as BAFS - Accounting elective in HKDSE) can pick it up easier.
sections.teaching: Prof Li tried to link the content of this course with the real life events as example, which maintains the interest of students. He balanced the contents and the students' workload.
sections.grading:
The grade is quite good.
The questions in the mid term test and final exam are similar to the in-class exercise. If you can finish and understand them, you could get a good grade for the course.
sections.workload:
1 Mid term test, 1 final exam.
Students are free to do the in-class exercise on board, or to present news for obtaining bonus point.
No assignment and no attendance taking.
The workload is small.

sections.content: Examination content is indeed very similar to those in the book. So practicing the exercises of the accounting book are more than enough to deal with the exams
sections.teaching: Li Xi generally gives great teaching. The teaching speed is relative low comparing to other instructors, so it is definitely good for accounting newbie. His notes encompass various out-sy but interesting financial accounting concepts and financial news. If you are interested in financial market, his notes might suit your appetite.
sections.grading:
I got A- with less than 1 sd higher than mean
Midterm mean = ~86
Final exam mean <70
sections.workload:
NO Homework and group project
Only mid term and final exams, very light workload patently

sections.content: The course is rather on fundamental accounting, like double entry, journal, financial statements etc.  Those who have studied BAFS Accounting before can pick up more easily.
sections.teaching: Tony is a comparatively good professor. His english is better than other acct professors (from what my friends and I have discovered) because of this many foreign students will take his course. But this brings another disadvantage : the foreign students will pull up the mean and SD because they have already learnt the materials taught in this course before. And although his English is good, his lessons grew boring afterwards.
sections.grading:
In my two exams,I got a score lower than the mean and got a C in the end.
But for studying his exam, he will always say to do exercise on the textbook. Do not do this, it is completely useless, the exercises are nothing like his paper. He is also unwilling to give out sample papers because he worries students will only study the sample papers.
sections.workload:
No assignments in his class, except for the optional homework.
One mid-term and one final
Some in-group exercise and quiz, the one with the lowest score will be taken off consideration of final score

sections.content: Li always talk about something not related to the course but he may teach you some skill on investing share as he used to teach based on the sources in financial time.
sections.teaching: quite good, he is willing to listen to others question and answer each question patiently. Willing to modify his teaching method.
sections.grading: emphasizes he will give as many A,B as he can,haha
sections.workload: no assignmentttttt and will not take attendenceeeee so what you need to do is go home and download all the powerpoint and read it yourself.

sections.content: The content of Acct 2010 is quite easy. it is only about the basic accounting and if you have the background of accounting, you can skip all the classes and still understand what's going on.
sections.teaching: Tony's teaching is quite good. However, he remembers the name of students. If you skip the class, he will know.
sections.grading: I have got a 98% in final but still got a B+ in acct. Since the paper was quite easy, many people can get a high mark and the mean is quite high.
sections.workload:
Only one mid term and several quizzes and group exercises. The final is non- cumulative.
Every quiz or group exercise will be notified by the professor a week before or a lesson before. So there will not be any pop up quizzes.

sections.content: An overview of the fundamentals of financial accounting. Content is clear and concise (but probably too little?) and can be easily understood by anyone with/without accounting background. Great for beginners.
sections.teaching: The professor can teach very clearly although it is not to say that he's a fun guy (lol, he can be pretty boring but I guess that doesn't really matter, as long as he can make the students understand the materials). He asks quite a number of questions and also interacts with students, so he's quite engaging.
sections.grading:
The exams are pretty easy, so it's really hard to get mean+SD, and there was one time when the mean+SD > 100% lol so yeah it's almost impossible

Mini quizzes are approx 40% of the total grade (my total is 114/120, with 40 total marks per quiz)
Final exam is <40%, got full mark
The rest of the grade is from attendance, cases (homework), and in-class exercises -- anyone could easily get 100% on these though
Final grade is A+
sections.workload: You need to do exercise in every lecture and he also gave 2 cases you need to work on with your group mate; there are also 3 mini quizzes and a final. However, I can say that the workload is pretty light and the problems he gave are quite easy. Finals and quizzes are pretty easy compared to other lectures too (which explains the high mean).

sections.content: 會教usa gaap system 既accounting, 同dse 既format唔太似，format要記過，有學過bafs 會有着數(如果你叻), 如果唔係就係簡單既本身唔識既好快明，難既你識唔識都係一樣咁學。
sections.teaching: 教學雖然唔太有趣，但勝在每樣野都好清晰，佢會1邊做落白紙，1邊ppt, 同你一路講1路做，專心有上堂，mid-term 同hw 一d 都唔難。
sections.grading:
好好grad
15% 1st mid-term
15% 2nd mid-term
25% Hw
5-8% Participation (攞卡，問/答問題，唔係1張1%,  唔知點judge)
(如果你Hw冇full, 而parti 又好先會多過5%,  hw+parti max.  30%)
