sections.workload: 6次hw, 佢只係計最高5次既分，頭5次full mark 可以揀唔做第6次

sections.content: The content taught in this course is the fundamentals required, i.e. the four statements in accounting, as well as how to draw and analyze the statements. They are not very hard if you follow the lecture notes and ppt. However, it would be a definite advantage to those who studies BAFS in high school.
sections.teaching: Prof Chen is quite good. Providing clear explanation through ppts and exercises, she can let students understand concepts clearly. She asks students to ask questions frequently, so they can get participation marks and understand what is taught in the lesson. She also tells some jokes and real life examples in the lecture to create a good learning atmosphere.
sections.grading:
The grading of this course is quite good. With satisfactory participation rate, i.e. one answer each lecture, mean score at each midterm and finals, and full mark in hw (all students get full marks so it is not hard at all), you can get a B+. It is not hard at all if you revise and participate.

Students who did accounting before have a great advantage and it is not hard to get A.
sections.workload: The workload is relatively low. Apart from the frequent hw (a total of 6 in the semester), the only thing left to do is to revise for the 2 midterms, which includes mc and lqs, and there are some hard questions. Students who studied accounting before will definitely handle the work better.

sections.content: Professor emphasizes combining both knowledge on class and real life examples. Thus he usually spends some time to explain on one or two related issues in every class. Generally speaking, the content would be okay for students who have taken bafs before in dse, only point to mention is that part of the entries are different from bafs, since this class uses American style accounting. However, non-bafs students might find it necessary to pay much effort to catch up.
sections.teaching: Professor Xi has a generally slower teaching pace than other classes, since he spends comparatively larger portion of time explaining real life examples. His lessons are usually in good pace, and students are generally attentive. Only few of the classes might be boring, but students still take initiative to ask questions.Both Professor Xi and the TA are very willing to answer questions on the discussion board of CANVAS.
sections.grading: In view of a bafs student, the levels of difficulty of the mid-term paper and final exam paper are generally acceptable , with the later more difficult. The SD of the class are generally high, and full marks are not impossible. Grades are good if you pay enough effort. Also, students who volunteer to give news presentations in front of the class or demonstrate completing in-class questions can obtain bonus marks.
sections.workload: No homework is given. All preparations and practices have to be done by yourself. There would only be mid-term, in-class exercises and final exams. It is suggested that students prepare the powerpoints or read the text book before class. Only materials covered in both ppt and textbooks would be in exam syllabus.

sections.content: Do not choose this instructor if you cannot stand a boring lesson. His tone is extremely flat. He will teach the hard knowledge by talking the powerpoint most of the time. He would teach for a hour first , then give you some time to finish the class works. These class works are also used to mark your attendance. He would let you form your own group and choose a good classmate can surely benefit your study in ACCT.
sections.teaching: His teaching is quite fast. He would read out the powerpoint and may be read out the example in the powerpoint then. His teaching is fully based on the powerpoint, But as he said, Acct is all about exercise. His teaching is not as matter as your self studying and exercising.
sections.grading: I got a C plus in this course. I had never studied Acct before. The mean of every test and exam is quite high in fact, may be around 80%. I got mean in average in the test and below 1 SD in exam. Others assignments and attendance are quite well.
sections.workload: His workload is not that heavy as he does not require us to do many homework. But the matter is others classmates work so hard that you have to follow suit. Otherwise, you will be out of the game in a not far future.

sections.content: don't take  Li Xi's lecture. Because it requires you to do project and during lecture, most of the content is related to finance and not really about how you deal with acct. But if you are really interested in how to apply acct and fina knowledge and do some case studies, it would be good to take his course.
sections.teaching: His english is quite good. He merely uses powerpoint slides to teach and most of the time he can make his points clear.
sections.grading: Most of the acct courses require students to score high because most of the students score high. If you cannot score higher than 1 sd, you cannot get good grade.
sections.workload: Have assignment every week.

sections.content:
Principles of Financial accounting, and mainly financial statements.
His powerpoint notes are basically summarized from the textbooks.
All the practice questions are from the textbooks.
sections.teaching:
Goes over powerpoint with notes every single classes.
Not particularly boring during the class, but you might get tired eventually.
He likes when you participate in his class, so make him remember your name.
sections.grading:
Attendance and Participation (5%)
In-Class Group Exercises (10%)
In-Class Quizzes (10%)
Mid-Term (35%)
Final (40%)

For the group exercises, it would obviously be better if you team up with your smart friends. We had total five group exercises, and although not mentioned in the syllabus, the professor dropped the lowest one.

For the in-class quizzes, he dropped the lowest one.

Mid term tended to be harder than the final. So prepare for the mid term.

One thing about grading for accounting is that one number error can screw the entire number, which TA, with too much workload, sometimes cannot find it and give you partial credit. So always check you quizzes or midterms if you can claim any more points.
sections.workload: Workload is decent. Just keep up on the reading and DO solve the assigned practice questions. He posts the answers for the practice questions. So if you can understand what is going on in the practice questions, you are good to go at least for the in class group exercises and quizzes.

sections.content:
Business school 第一個sem必修嘅course. 對於有DSE Bafs Account背景嘅人會有較明顯嘅優勢(特别係頭幾課).個course主要係教accounting嘅basic野,例如基本嘅accounting concepts,點樣畫d常用嘅accounts(e.g income statement, balance sheet, etc), account  ing equations等等, 大部份都係有account底嘅人學過嘅,所以會比其他人事半功倍,但注意ust教嘅account係美國版,而DSE account係用國際版,所以部份topic嘅做法會有出入(e.g bad debts).
唔同DSE, 個course考concept多過畫表同計數.
利申: DSE BAFS Account 5** (非晒名)
sections.teaching:
教得幾有心,幾nice,雖然有時幾悶,但睇得出佢想令到個lecture有趣d,好樂意解答同學嘅問題.主要都係跟textbook教
兩個TA效率幾慢,考完mid term成個月都未改晒lol.
聽聞佢係爛grade嘅,但我最後拎左個A,所以請大家自行判斷
sections.grading:
Class activities and participation (10%): 自行分組(5-6人),堂上做textbook入面嘅題目,本身一早講定邊堂lecture做class work同做邊題.話就話堂上做,但通常都係做唔切,可以下堂先交番. 同時呢個都係識fd唔錯嘅機會
Case about ethics in accounting (15%): Individual嘅功課,會俾個情景你,要你講個情景犯左咩accounting ethics同點解決d問題,DSE冇乜讀過呢d野,自己做到一頭霧水.最後冇派番份功課,幾多分都唔知.
Mid-term exam (25%): 30條mc佔60%,考concept居多,計數題少; Long q佔40%,包括畫accounts(包括Journal),計數同文字題.整體唔太難
Final exam (50%):non-cumulative,即係唔會考番mid-term前嘅syllabus,形式同mid-term差唔多,會比mid-term難,好大程度上因為後期教嘅野難d,DSE account 考生都未學過.考試時間充裕. 最後都係都知final嘅result
sections.workload:
正如頭先講過,個course對有account背景嘅人都幾着數,基本上考試前溫一晚就ok, 而class work都唔係太難,因為textbook嘅example都幾多,更何況有d人可能本身有textbook solution.反而係份individual功課要認真做.
至於對冇account底嘅人黎講,就要努力少少,畢竟本身我自己中學開頭讀bafs嗰陣都要一段時間先清到account嘅概念. 一開頭不妨請教下高中有讀過account嘅同學,咁樣會幫到你地清下concept,否則之後唔係咁易跟得上.

sections.content: Notes are easy to understand and main points from textbook are covered in the notes.
sections.teaching:
Teaching and notes are clear and easy to follow.
Quick and detailed responds are given in Discussion on Canvas.
sections.grading:
Cheat sheets are allowed in both mid-terms and final.
Participation is the bonus mark. Asking and answering questions are easy.
But, final is quite difficult compared to other classes.
I got higher marks in the 2 mid-term(nearly full mark) and full mark in all the HWs. But I didn't  do well in final. Still got B+.
sections.workload:
6 HW in total, all are group projects
2 mid-term exams. Don't worry they are easy. Hints are given and questions are similar to those in textbook(exactly the same questions but changing the numbers). So you just need to do more textbook exercises in order to get higher marks.

sections.content: seems not so hard comparing to others, design and the arrangement of the notes is perfect
sections.teaching: easy to understand the concepts behind,design and the arrangement of the notes is perfect
sections.grading: the quiz and final are easy,so you have to attain a very high score in order to get a A/B range
sections.workload: Not much in HW. but there are 3 quizes each semester replacing the midterm, no worries, those quizes are easy and just like those in the textbook exercises, so just finish the exercises/practice from the professor and u can get good marks

sections.content: Basic accounting principle,since the definition of terms is not examined,understanding on the topic is more important.Mainly discuss how we record the journal entries for different transaction, and how we present them on financial statement.The content of the course is quite simple.
sections.teaching: The teaching style is quite relax, the teacher would ask question to students, and encourage students to ask question. His teaching is clear and will let you know which part is not required or not important. It is easy to follow the lecture with different examples in lecture notes. Attendance of class is very important since every in-class exercise carries points for final grade.
sections.grading:
Don't know much on grading since I don't know how others' grades are.But I think that the grading is fair for me.

sections.workload: The workload is very light,there would be three mini-exam which covers up to three chapter individually. The cases are not very difficult and would not take you much time to work on.

the ppt was not simple enough and quite hard to understand
His coverage is also more and harder than other professors, so if you are really interested in accountings His course will be good for you.
No attendance is taken but he does remember people's name, even if you never speak. He will ask for your reason of absence. Also due to the numerous quizzes and assignments in class, you can hardly skip lesson. So don't try skipping his classes.

lecture + class exercises.

class exercises help a lot

three mini exams and final exam are difficult and short of time

sections.workload:
Three mini exams (40 points each)
two cases analysis
Final exam (cumulative, 115 points out of 300 total)

sections.content: Professor was teaching according to the PowerPoint slide with details, seldom talked about anything out of scope, while sometimes used some daily example to show us how things work. There's around 10 chapters in total and are almost similar to what the textbook is providing. This course is a fundamental course for accounting, therefore it might be beneficial for someone who has studied account previously in high school. There are some financial content as well, but they are quite easy to be understood.
sections.teaching: Professor Chen never talked too fast or too slow, he used most of the lecture time to talk about the content of the slides while sometimes he would do some examples to show us the methodology behind. He would answer questions from students, rather it is face to face or via email. You can even find him at his office on the given office hour, he would still kindly answer you inquiries even it's not his office hour though. He knew that some of us might not have been studying accounting before, he described every little point with detail. I'm sure that even you haven't studied accounting before, you will have no problem in understanding most of the course.
sections.grading:
Homework 10%
Mid-term 40%
Final 50%
That might be a huge weighted score for exam, but the difficulties of the exam is average, it is similar to what the textbook have, should  you practice more with your textbook, the exam would be easy for you. There are MCs in the exams, but they were straight forward and nothing really conceptual. The use of his words in the exam is clear enough, college student shouldn't be confused at all.
sections.workload: He gave 10 homework assignments in total, which are given after he finishes a chapter. The answer of the assignment need not be correct, but you should show your passion in doing it! Usually it's a one-question assignment, and nothing else needed to be done.

sections.content:
Intro
Balance Sheet
Income Statement

Revenue Recognition
Inventory
LT assets
Liabilities and time value

covered quite a lot of topics compared to some other sessions
sections.teaching:
The teaching pace was a bit fast but one should be able to follow if u pay attention. The prof. would tryto cover as many topics as possible and expect you to go through the details on textbook by yourself.

PPT slides are well organized and concise. Taught according to ppt, and would quote textbook examples or her own examples for demonstration in class.

Asking questions in class is strongly encouraged, and the prof would also answer students' questions on canvas discussion board
sections.grading:
22-25% Homework
5-8% Class Participation
15% Midterm 1
15% Midterm 2
40% Final

Mean for the two midterms were about 75-85%, but the mean of final exam was below 50%
sections.workload:
Homework:
6 group homework, counts the best 5
Usually 2-3 questions which are not very difficult
and you can find similar question types on textbook
Groups are assigned by the professor, around 5-6 ppl per group

Participation:
need to ask questions or answer questions to gain participation cards

Exams:

MC (emphasizes the conceptual details), Short questions with calculations, and some complex long questions in final

Some of the midterm questions were modified from textbook exercise, it is recommended to get a textbook for self practice to prepare for exam.

Content of final exam is cumulative. And cheatsheets are allowed for both midterm and final.

sections.content:
Basic Accounting knowledge which stress on the accounting mechanism.

Similar to HKDSE BAFS, with some minor differences, mainly becuase they are following two different accounting standard.
sections.teaching:
Prof. Shieh has taught this course for a long time (both in UST, cityu), so he understands what students are struggling about most of the time.

Concepts are illustrarted by different examples in the boon, which are useful, especially for those who do not know accounting at all.

Good presentation with cute voice, feel that he teaches with and by heart. If you attend all the lectures, most probably you will understand the basic techniques.

Prof. Shieh has been to HK from Taiwan for more than twenty years, he speaks English, Cantonese and Putonghua in a extremely fluent way (he knows what you are talking in Cantonese, don't try to say anything bad). No difficulties In understanding his words. You may speak in one of the three languages mentioned after class, in case of any questions.

Anyway, heard from friends that their prof are some how difficult to understand, if you don't think you are smart enough to understand things easily, enroll in his class. :)
sections.grading:
Fair grading, your effort will paid off.
1 * Midterm (94.5/100) (mean 69,sd 18)
1* final (95/100) (mean 81)
3 *quizzes ( drop the lowest one) (10/10 for 2 counted)
5* inclass group ex (10/10 for all)

Turns up A+, heard from previous years that he distributed quite a lot A range and C range

Again, work hard, you will get what you pay
sections.workload:
For midterm and final, he is quite different from other professors, his exams are similar to DSE( paper 2A) and AL, in terms of format. NO MCQs in both exams, all are structured questions which requires you to set up account/ compute. While each questions will consists of some concept sub questions( i.e. You have to write some sentences and apply acconting concepts in the case), but most important things is the work concerning account/statement/ computation. Textbook will be good for you.

Both examinations are not really difficult if you get all the concepts in the powerpoint, comparing to other professors, at least (other lectures' students look horrible after final)

Quizzes sometimes are difficult, inclass group exercises are not really hard. Good to have a student who have learned accounting before.

sections.content: Simple account...even without any account ratios...The concept is easy but it's not really the same with HKDSE syllabus...
sections.teaching:
I think Tony taught a bit fast...you may need to review the content in leisure time if you want to fully understand...the time on the lesson is hard for you to understand the concept clearly.
However, Tony explains and teaches very clearly and you just need time but it's generally easy to understand.
Some schoolmates reflect that other prof. can hardly explain that clearly and it's hard for them to understand...I'm not sure.
sections.grading:
Fair grading.
He will surely consider your attendance by watching your photos in class to determine who is in the classes hahaha
sections.workload:
Not many workload.
Some group-exercise which don't need much preparation.
Quizzes should be seriously treated...
The examinations are quite different with other classes but it's not really difficult.

sections.content: Content of this course provides the basic understanding of accounting. It is also easy for the beginners to understand. However, it gets slightly difficult towards the end when the chapters get related to each other.
sections.teaching: Professor Tony is great, he has humor ad great English as well. However, his teaching is very unique among the other ACCT2010 professors, so it is little difficult to compare our work with others.
sections.grading: I think grading is good. I managed to received A. However, it is important to note that if you mess your mid term or final, you will really slip in your grade. Doing well in quiz and group exercise will not make a significant impact on your grade.
sections.workload:
Workload is fairly good. There are several group exercises and quiz, but for group exercises we can ask him for any doubts. I had only 3 quiz throughout the term. Preparation is really easy because you only need to do the book exercises. Also, you can drop the lowest score for the quiz as well as the group exercise.

Professor Tony also separates the syllabus for mid term and final exams.

His presentation is not bad at all but if you are the first time listening to accounting lecture, you might be confused.
He does not allow computers, phones or any electronic devices in the class, even to take picture or to see ppt. He demands you to print required ppt every chapter.
sections.grading:

sections.content: Compulsory course for business students, very basic financial accounting, should have no problem to understand the course content.
sections.teaching: Prof Li not only teaches accounting in class. He also discuss something related to the current financial markets to us, which I think was quite interesting.
sections.grading: 45%midterm and 55% final. No assignments, projects whatever at all. Very good grade. He said in the first class that he will give the best grade allowed by the University, and he did. I was above mean 2/3 SD in both midterm and final, and got A-.
sections.workload: Almost zero workload. All you need to do is to attend all lectures, spend several hours to go through the in-class exercises before exams, and that will suffice.

Mainly about the preparation of financial statements. The topics overlaps most the DSE content, except the statement of cash flow.

Having studied in BAFS in high school is an advance, but be careful that the format of the financial statements may not be exactly the same.
sections.teaching: Monotone, but very clear pronunciation, at least better than many Mainland professors. If you pay attention in class, you will have no difficulty on understanding what he said.
sections.grading:

sections.content: Content in the course is appropriate for an introduction to accounting, but, be advised, that if you do not have an accounting background, you will find it a little tough in the first few lectures of the semester. Basic concepts include journal entries, depreciation, balance sheet, income statement, statement of cash flow, dividends, bonds, etc.
sections.teaching: Mostly PowerPoint based - helps if you do the readings of the PPT before class begins. Aside from that, heavy reliance on the cases from GOME / Apple, to consolidate all the knowledge obtained from the classes, and apply them tor all financial statements.
sections.grading:
Grading for this course - mean is generally in the low 80s / high 70s, since lots of people already have some level of accounting background, and therefore the means generally become high.

Neither examination is really that hard, and if prepared well enough, then it is not hard to score well on these examinations.
sections.workload: Optional homework given based off the concepts covered in class, quizzes and in class exercises here and there which require little preparation. One midterm, one final, and one ethics report (3 pages). Workload not high.

sections.content:
The syllasbus of the courese have almost been covered by dse level in bafs. So students who studied bafs would have advantages. But i think this course is quite straight forward and easy to understand for those who do not take bafs. But still so effort should be put in doing exercises.

sections.content: Very detailed content, each of the chapters covered in class is very informative. Class presentations for each chapter are uploaded on Canvas, as well as in-class exercises taken from the textbook. A very comprehensive and thorough introduction to financial accounting, and a useful course for beginners.
sections.teaching: Teaching is relatively good, however for students without previous accounting background, it's quite tough in the beginning because the content is covered quite quickly. However, the teacher is patient with answering questions about the course material. There are also plenty of opportunities for you to ask questions, and gain participation cards.
sections.grading: The mean for the midterms is very high, as there are many students with prior knowledge about the subject (from DSE or A-Levels). Standard deviation is also pretty low for both of the midterms. Do your best in the homework assignments, and try to get a lot of participation cards.
sections.workload: There are 6 homework assignments to be completed in a homework group with 4-5 other students, and the 5 assignments with the highest marks will be taken into grade consideration. It's advisable to do all the suggested problems, as similar questions appear in the midterms. The final requires extensive knowledge of all the syllabus content though, and requires you to prepare full financial statements.

not too difficult

his english is easy to understand

sections.content: ACCT 2010 is definitely where you want to get your basics for accounting, and Tony Shieh is definitely a good lecturer to get your basics right. We looked at financial statements and learned what some terms meant, what the numbers indicated, etc etc. Definitely a good course to get you introduced to the applications of financial accounting--one that every basic financial statement user (external) needs.
sections.teaching: Tony Shieh definitely knows his stuff. He's currently the Academic Director of MSc in Accounting here at UST, and teaches in great detail. He's very open to questions and very approachable in and outside class. If you don't understand something, he'd gladly go over the material again as per request.
sections.grading: Grading is definitely competitive, but this is mainly because a lot of the students enrolled in ACCT 2010 have some accounting background back in high school. Even so, the course is generally lenient in terms of grades.
sections.workload: Workload is quite a lot. There are a bunch of quizzes and group exercises, but he doesn't grade the worst one. The quizzes are generally easier than the group exercises, since the former count more towards your grade than the latter. There's also a group project, and you're required to make a short report in groups of 4. It's not that hard, and a guide is provided to help you write it out.

sections.content: Very good. Not covering all content in the textbook, though. No homework. Only group work which is in class exercise.
sections.teaching: Very patient and elaborative. Use online forum to answer all questions. Sometimes might be a bit difficult to follow because of the instructor's accent and low tone when speaking.
sections.grading: I got more than 1sd above mean in midterm. All participation and group work full marks. Did not do well in final, which was extremely difficult. Got A- at last.
sections.workload: Higher than the average of 3-cred courses. Need to get very clear idea about the concepts. Should do a lot of practices.

This is an introductory course of financial accounting.
If you have studied BAFS in DSE, it is very easy to get an A cuz many of the topics have learnt already.

sections.content: A lot of finance knowledge accompanied with basic accounting. Quite demanding for me but certainly worth studying.
sections.teaching: The professor is used to explain theories with real business cases, which in my point of view, makes the classes more vivid. More than that, we are required to present a company analysis in the end of the course in teams, which adds real practice and team corporation into the lesson.
sections.grading: It is said that the professor graded a great number of A range.
sections.workload: I find it a little burdening regarding the pre-class exercise, a lot to write.

sections.content: If you have studied BAFS in high school, then you would have no problem understanding the concepts and contents covered in this course. It starts from the basics (dr and cr) etc.
sections.teaching: Prof. Shieh is super friendly and are very willing to answer any questions raised. Also, he explained concepts and principles very clearly. He would ask each group to stand in front of the whiteboard to take a photo with your name on top, so he could remember most of our names.
sections.grading: I think Prof. Shieh follow the school's grading policy. Asking questions in class would definitely give you bonus points as he would be able to recognise you from the photos and give you participation points.
sections.workload: There is a midterm and final (contents are not cumulated). Also there's a case study that you have to finish in groups, but a really short one, so the workload is average.

sections.content: The ppts written by Prof Chen are very clear and easy to understand, which truly facilitate revision.
sections.teaching: Professor Chen is very friendly and is always willing to answer students' questions. She is also very passionate about teaching, always attempting to engage students and helping weaker students in answering her questions (everyone in her class has to answer 5 questions raised by the prof throughout the semester for class participation).
sections.grading: The final was shockingly hard, especially when compared to the midterm exam, and even those who took BAFS as an elective in high school found it difficult. Despite so, the percentage of students getting an A-range is high.
sections.workload: The workload is light, without any homework but only weekly in-class exercises.

sections.content:
Basic accounting concept, appropriate for those who have not learned anything about accounting stuffs.

It basically teaches you about how to make financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, and statement of cashflows) using various types of standards (GAAP and IFRS). It also teaches you about how to write an entry journal and trial balance.

Also explains about each component of the financial statements, but not in a detailed one.
sections.teaching:
Perfect teaching! Really love how he teaches.

Good knowledge, lenient teachers, he builds the spirit in the class. He uses ppt and basically refers to the ppt, but he always adds some of his experiences, or explains more about the ppt. Ppt is very readible.

Professor is also open to questions and discussions in class.
sections.grading:
Pretty lenient, I guess. Since there are many quizzes and in-class exercises, only 2-3 of your best will be taken, thus it will be easier to get a perfect score.

No idea about how he grade the class participation and group project, as scores will not be given to us for them.

Final and mid-term are a little bit tricky, but if you understand this course really well, it is pretty easy to get a very high score.

40% from final, 30% from midterm, 5% of class participation (basically you should be more active and ask questions if you want to get full score from this), 15% from quizzes and in-class exercise, 10% from projects that you do with your group
sections.workload:
There will be around 3-4 quizzes (individually, close book), and 4-5 in-class exercise (work in a group, open book) throughout the whole semester.

1 midterm with 5 essay questions (usually to make financial statements and do calculations), 1 final with 6-7 questions (non-cumulative)

Also, there will be 1 study case that will be done per group which we can choose by our own who will be in the same group with us.

sections.content: The content are mostly basic accounting such as adjustments and journal entry. Most of the material are already thought in highschool, except for the late chapters.
sections.teaching: Prof tony is really funy and d dicated. You could always make an apointment with him to dicuss the materials regarding with the course. He also pays attention toward the students
sections.grading: The grading ispretty tough. The mean is high, around 75% but you could easily get 80% if you study and pay attention to the lectures. The question are relatively easy, but a bit tricky.
sections.workload: The workload is quite heavy. Youvwill got a lot of quizes.

sections.content: Simple to understand with clear explanations of powerpoint.
sections.teaching: Willing to answer students' questions after class. He is funny with adequate jokes to keep the atmosphere of the class
sections.grading: Seems good in general with high percentage of students getting good grades.
sections.workload: 1 group project, 1 mid term and final exam respectively, 5 group exercise and 3 quizzes. No too much workload. It is quite flexible in workload because the professor might adjust the number of exercises or quizzes according to the preference of students. You can ask your friends to go in a same group with you.

sections.content:
The course is mainly about the basic knowledge of Accounting.
Maybe the content will be similar with the things you learn in secondary school accounting lessons. I think the class exercise, group work are really helpful to deepen your understanding.
sections.teaching: Peter chen is a funny instructor with his stylish English. As he comes from the mainland, his English is not quite accurate and the accent is different from Hong Kong too. Therefore, you may find difficult to understand what he say.
sections.grading: The grading scheme is absolutely fantastic, as it only count on the group work you have done , mid-term and final. I got an A+ finally
sections.workload: The workload is very light, as the class exercise and group work is easy enough. In Peter's class, there is no group project and participation mark. Therefore, the course is really relax, and you just need to revise the material precisely. Then, you can get a good grade

sections.content:
Its useful and you will understand the basic theories behind those complicated annual reports.

Students who have studied BAFS will have some advantage - the theories are the same but the methods of how to deal with the problems are a bit different so its recommended for those who studied before should attend lectures as well.
sections.teaching: Prof. You is a mainland prof and he was graduated from a US school so no problem for students to understand his lecture. Also, he taught very clearly so that you can easy to understand - the best thing is - he will tell you the difficult part in advance so that you can have a look before his lecture. Moreover, after his lecture, he would say' oh this part is very important in the acct system' and you will know that that part must be tested.
sections.grading: Many mainland students would register for his course and that's why the mean of the course is quite high but the grade is also good - appx. 20% A range and most of my local friends at least got B range.
sections.workload:
2 mid term exams + 1 final exam - the first one with many ppl got full mark, but the nightmare was that the second one was much more difficult and many people suffered because they still thought that it would be easy

For the final exam, as prof You did mention at his last lecture, thats much more difficult and the mean was 8x/120 comparing to 10x/120 in the previous mid term exams.

So be careful of the last two tests and dont skip lectures

There are some in-class quiz, basically that would be the first lecture of week has no quiz and the second lecture has.

sections.content: All fundamental accounting stuffs. I would say that the content is quite packed, and the pace of the lecture is quite fast. So, having previous knowledge of accounting before taking this course would be a great advantage.
sections.teaching:
Prof CHEN, Zhihong is a very great professor. I like his  teaching style very much. He gave us a preview questions (required, counted as assignments) of new materials that are going to be discussed in the class. He wanted us to at least do a preview ourselves, and try to solve the problem. I found this very useful, since it actually helps us to understand better and faster during his lecture.
Prof also gave a series of selected problem sets from the textbook that he recommended us to do it. This is where the textbook comes in handy, since one of the essay questions in the exam was taken from the textbook. (The rest exam questions was actually harder than the textbook problem sets, but doing all them will help you understand the accounting concept much easier, which will eventually help you do the exams.)
sections.grading: The grade are distributed between the 3 lectures Prof CHEN, Zhihong was teaching that time. Fair grading, the final letter grade was heavily determined by mid and final exams. I think, having a grade in the mean range will be enough to get you at least a B-.
sections.workload: Low workload, we just have to submit through LMES the required questions every time before the class starts.

sections.content: Basic concepts of Accounting. Most of the topics are included in the HKDSE curriculum. So foe HKDSE students who take BAFS as their elective subject shd be very capable to get an A range in this course, no matter who the instructor is.
sections.teaching: He explained the concepts in a very clear way. Very easy to understand the basic principles of accounting for the beginners.
sections.grading:
very good grade ar!
My mid term, quiz are all above mean about 1 sd, but my final was just over mean a bit. But I still got an A!.
sections.workload: Very low workload. Only three quizzes. The quizzes are very easy to get full marks.

sections.content: The content of this course is about the foundation of Accounting. Indeed it favours the ones who have studied BAFS/ Accounting in the past, it is quite easy to master for those who have no Accounting knowledge.
sections.teaching: Professor Chen taught well and the teaching materials he has prepared are easy to understand. He would demonstrate some questions in the class which makes us know better about the topics.
sections.grading: The grading of Professor Chen is really good. Many people got B range although they scored below the median.
sections.workload: The workload was very light. There were only 10 group assignments submitted in the semester, while the assignments were similar to the ones he demonstrated in class. There were also no quiz nor project. Therefore, Peter's class was considered to be a relaxing one.

sections.content: Content is very standard and basic stuff. Journal entries, balance sheets, income statements, statement of cash flows, and statement of stockholders' equity. Just be aware of not balancing everything because of a small mistake...
sections.teaching: Peter has very solid knowledge of accounting, but he has an accent, and talks EXTREMELY SLOW. Accounting is very boring stuff, so it can get very sleepy during lectures.
sections.grading: Grading is fair (I guess), because he (or his TA) did not release the final exam scores, but I got into A range by getting 1 SD above mean in the mid-term and missed the whole final question on the final exam, so grading should be fair.
sections.workload: Workload is EXTREMELY small. Peter gives in-class exercises during lectures (practice is very important when learning accounting), and there are 10 very easy group homework assignments. Mid-term and final exams included.

sections.content: Introduction to the concepts and principles of financial accounting, including the analysis, recording, and reporting of business transactions and preparation of financial statements like opening T-account, balance sheet and income statement.
sections.teaching: He teaches easy things with clear explanations. He also teaches about the real business situation.
sections.grading: since the exam and mid-term are super easy, all students could get high marks. Therefore, even people get very high marks , they can't get a high grade.

for a BAFS student, you can easily handle the course.

7-8 hw

One midterm and One final for Prof. Chen. Different from other classes that I heard, they had two or more midterm and quiz. It's more risky compare to other profs lecture.
Also, FINAL EXAM was much difficult than anyone expected.
And I didn't get back my final exam grade but its far better than my expectation.

Teaching about fundamental concepts of basic accounting.

The lesson is a bit boring but the concepts is welly explained.
For peter's lesson, he will teach about the concepts in the first half of the lesson and then he will finish the in-class exercise together with the class in the second half of the lesson.
sections.grading:
One mid-term and one final for Peter's lecture.

For the final, the mean is around 80/115.
I got 90% of the total marks and received an A+ for this course.

sections.content: Not very difficult as long as you have taken BAFS accounting as your elective in secondary school.
sections.teaching: Fair.  Not very clear sometimes but she will make sure all of us understand the contents.  She will always ask us whether the class is going to fast and make the corresponding adjustment.
sections.grading: The grading is quite good even though the final is very difficult.  Got an A.
sections.workload: It is fair.  Just need to hand in a class worksheet at the end of each lesson.  It can be done by yourself or forming a group.  Also, there is 5% for the class participation and you just need to take 5 cards during the lessons.  As long as you try, you can get a card.  The professor will give you tips always.

sections.content: Actually it's easy if you have studied accounting before. It is just a brief introduction on accounting and starts from zero. However, it is taught in american style accounting system so some may find it in a mess.
sections.teaching: Although it's hard to listen clearly from his accent, he's still a good teacher who teaches step by step with clear and useful PowerPoint notes.
sections.grading: Just follow the grading standard from mainstream. Probably you will be in A range if you are above 1 SD in both midterm and final.
sections.workload: Light workload which only have group assignment per week. More than that is only midterm and final.

sections.content: The content is quite good, some examples shown in the ppt,  with some step-to-step teaching. If you have study accounting before, the ppt is adequate for you to study, but the one who never study BAFs, I recommend you to buy a textbook to do more exercise, which is quite good for your study. However it is quite often of having some typo in the ppt and class review problem, so be careful for this.
sections.teaching: The professor's teaching is quite boring, and the ppt used is with black background and white word, it is quite difficult to see and not printer-friendly. I have played truant several times, I think it is okay for you not to attend if you know enough about content.
sections.grading:
The grading is quite good if you have study BAFs in high school. In both mid-terms and final, there is one question is taken from the practice problem, so the one who is not very good at it can study more from the practice problem. Cheat sheet is allowed in both mid-term and final.

Grading:
Instructor's discretion (base on class behaviour) - 10%
Class participation (homework, no attendance) - 10%
Mid-term (2 mid-terms) - 2*20% = 40%
Final - 40%
sections.workload: If you have study BAFs in secondary school, it would be quite easy to finish the homework. Each lecture needs to hand in 2-3 questions homework, which you need to preview the new chapter. However, it may be a bit difficult for those who never take BAFs. And the homework won't be graded, you only need to hand in, so the workload is not very heavy.

sections.content: It may be quite difficult for beginners without any accounting background to pickup at first. There are many specific terms related to accounting that must be first understood. After you understand the basics, the rest is pretty easy to follow.
sections.teaching:
One of the worst professors I had this semester. I'm not one to skip classes (usually) but I really did not want to attend this professors lessons. It was difficult to understand her, and she does go through things too quickly. I would sit through the whole lesson and listening to what she was trying to teach but still end up not understanding a single thing. Then she expects us to do in-class exercises to show her what we have learnt but how can I show what I have learnt when I learnt nothing at all?

She will answer any questions you ask on LMES discussion board pretty quickly though.
sections.grading: Fair. Not especially good grade.
sections.workload:
Workload is not that much. It is okay to just focus on midterm and finals. She claims that she cares about participation (i.e doing in-class exercises each week, and talking in class to get cards) but it didn't really affect my grade.

Midterm was pretty easy but final was a different story. It is nothing like what you will go through in class.

sections.content: Comparing to all other professors, Dr. Chen put a lot more emphasis on theory understanding rather than the high school type of memorizing formats of statements. A lot more effort in revising is required than other sections.
sections.teaching: Use an approach which hopes you to understand the theory behind every concept. Spends a lot of time after class and in-class to cope with students' problems. Tries a lot to engage students into the class.
sections.grading:
Would be at least OK if you have studied related subjects before (e.g. BAFS), because it is too difficult for those without any knowledge to catch up. Mid term is ok, but final is a lot more deeper into the concepts and to the real world situation, where you would be given a lot of reality-like statement which are very disturbing to read.
P.S. B+
sections.workload: 0 Workload except in-class excercise.

sections.content: Basic Financial Accounting. If you have taken BAFS (Accounting Module) before, this course would definitely be easy for you.

Peter teaches well and elaborates clearly on every steps of accounting entries.

sections.teaching: Allen is really a good professor in terms of his teaching and his look :) (i'm sorry girls he is already married). Interesting examples during class and many fitness tips ;p
sections.grading: Allen is good grade though his final is a bit difficult. Doing more exercise in textbook should help in getting good grade.
sections.workload: No homework, some class exercise. suggest reading through the chapters in txtbk to get a better understanding.  Preparing for midterms and finals can be tough since it requires lots of exercise.

sections.content: I will say there's some advantages that exist for those who have prior accounting knowledge as this course is really at the introductory level. Remarkably however, this course adopts a slightly different approach than the usual IFRS. The course used GAAP so it may take some time for one to adapt to GAAP.
sections.teaching: Peter's English was not that fluent. Occasionally, he may swap to Chinese for better expression. Notwithstanding, you may refer to the PPT that he made for reference. Those PPTs were quite useful.
sections.grading:
Peter Chen gave very good grades.Personally, i scored below mean in my mid-term examination and above mean 1 SD in final examination. I got a Level B+.
The thing is the grading method of this course is weird. 40% mid term, 45% final and 15% course work.
sections.workload: Basically no take-home assignments and no projects. Only have in-class http://assignments.As soon  as you can find good group mates, that would be fine.
